# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

"aipocalypse" — a PC first-person shooter built in Unity **6000.6.4f1** (Unity 6) with URP 17.6. Development happens in the Unity Editor; the `*.csproj`/`*.slnx` files at the repo root are generated by Unity — never edit them.

**Editor control: Unity CLI** (`unity`, via the `com.unity.pipeline` package). The deprecated Unity MCP is not used. The `unity-pipeline` skill in `.claude/skills/` is a copy of the one shipped in `Library/PackageCache/com.unity.pipeline@*/.claude/skills/` — refresh it when the package updates. The `tools-unity-*` / `eng-unity-*` skills are vendored from [tjboudreaux/cc-plugin-unity-gamedev](https://github.com/tjboudreaux/cc-plugin-unity-gamedev) (MIT) and are generic. Where they conflict with this file or `docs/technicals/`, the project docs win. `tools-unity-behavior-designer` has been rewritten for Behavior Designer Pro 3.3.3 and this architecture.

- Use `unity command <name>` to drive the live editor (scenes, GameObjects, components, prefabs, assets, captures, console) instead of hand-editing `.unity`/`.prefab`/`.asset` YAML. `unity command` lists all commands; follow the `unity-pipeline` skill (recompile → `recompile_status` → `run_tests` loop, `run_script` for bulk/plugin work, `eval` for one-liners).
- In Git Bash pass `--project-path "$(cygpath -w "$PWD")"` — the CLI doesn't match `/d/...` paths.
- Before editor work run `unity status` and `unity command set_autotick --enable true` (commands stall while Unity is unfocused otherwise); if not ready, check Safe Mode (`unity pipeline list`) or ask the user to open the project.
- Verify changes with `recompile_status` / `console` / `capture_scene_view` instead of guessing. Tests use `com.unity.test-framework` (`unity command run_tests`).

## Where things live

- `Assets/_Game/` — **all first-party game code and content go here.** Stable mechanics live in `Assets/_Game/_Core/` (one folder per system plus `_Bootstrap`, `_Common`, `_Debug`); design-dependent rules in `Assets/_Game/Features/`; trial mechanics in `Assets/_Game/_Experimental/`. Features depend on Core, never the reverse (enforced by asmdefs). ScriptableObject assets go in `Assets/_Game/Data/`. Full layout and system ownership: `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- `Assets/_Game/Scenes/Prototypes/` — `Proto_*` scenes that test one mechanic each, not in Build Settings. They use the real code and prefabs, never copies (rules in ARCHITECTURE.md → "Prototypes → main game").
- `Assets/_StoreAssets/` — third-party art/asset-store content (Synty Polygon Generic/Prototype, Low Poly Weapon Bundles 1–3, Stylized Grass/Water 3, Damage Numbers Pro, Feel). Treat as vendor code: don't modify; reference or make variants/prefabs under `_Game`.
- `Assets/Plugins/` — third-party editor/runtime tooling (Odin Inspector, DOTween/Demigiant, GPUInstancerPro, etc.). Don't modify.
- `Assets/Settings/` — URP assets (`PC_RPAsset`, `PC_Renderer`), volume profile, and Input System config.
- `Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity` — the only scene in Build Settings so far. `Assets/_Game/Scenes` is intended for real game scenes (add them to Build Settings when created).
- `Packages/` — local packages: A* Pathfinding Project (`com.arongranberg.astar`) and GPU Instancer Pro (`com.gurbu.gpui-pro` + prefab/terrain modules).

## Key tech choices (from `Packages/manifest.json`)

- **Input**: new Input System only (`activeInputHandler: 1`). Actions asset is `Assets/Settings/InputSystem_Actions.inputactions` with a `Player` map: Move, Look, Attack, Interact, Crouch, Jump, Previous, Next, Sprint. Use these actions; don't call the legacy `UnityEngine.Input`.
- **Architecture / DI**: VContainer (`jp.hadashikick.vcontainer`) + UniTask. Cross-system events go through MessagePipe. No `X.Instance` singletons in game code — services are plain C# registered in lifetime scopes; each system registers through its own installer. Entity prefabs (player, enemies…) carry their own `EntityScope` and must work dropped into any scene. See `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Enemy navigation**: A* Pathfinding Project 
- **Camera**: Cinemachine 6.6 is installed.
- **Rendering/perf**: URP, GPU Instancer Pro for foliage/props, VFX Graph, Splines, Terrain Tools.
- **Editor conveniences**: Odin Inspector (`Sirenix`), DOTween, Feel (MoreMountains), Damage Numbers Pro are available for game code.

## Plugins — check before building, use them correctly

Many runtime and editor plugins are installed (Feel, BroAudio, Easy Save 3, Damage Numbers Pro, DOTween, Odin, GPU Instancer Pro, A*, Unity Behavior, Localization…). **Read `docs/technicals/PLUGINS.md` before any task that a plugin might cover.**

- **Check first:** before writing a system or tool, check whether an installed plugin already does it. Use the plugin rather than reinventing it, unless PLUGINS.md says otherwise.
- **Use it the documented way:** follow the plugin's rules in PLUGINS.md (e.g. no plugin singletons/static event systems in gameplay code, `TimeService` owns `Time.timeScale`, uGUI for UI, DOTween for code tweens, Behavior only for unique AI). When unsure how a plugin works, read its docs or source in `Assets/Plugins/` / `Packages/` instead of guessing (some ship their own guide, e.g. `Assets/Plugins/BroAudio/CLAUDE.md`).
- **Use it efficiently:** prefer the plugin's pooling, batching and caching features (Damage Numbers Pro and BroAudio pooling, GPUI instancing) and keep per-instance plugin components off crowd entities.
- **Keep PLUGINS.md current:** when adding, removing or starting to use a plugin in a new way, update it in the same change.

## Keeping docs current

- When you add or change a core system (data structures, gameplay flow, system boundaries), update the relevant section of this file or `docs/` in the same change. Keep this file high-level; put detail in `docs/`.
- `docs/gdd/` — game design. Design intent: `docs/gdd/GDD.md` is the index of per-topic files; start with `docs/gdd/CORE.md` (pitch, pillars, core loop). `docs/gdd/IDEAS.md` is a draft scratchpad, not canon — never implement from it unless explicitly asked.
- `docs/technicals/` — technical docs. Architecture and data flow: `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Plugin usage rules: `docs/technicals/PLUGINS.md`. 
- Current milestone/tasks: `docs/ROADMAP.md`.
- A Stop hook (`.claude/hooks/check-docs.sh`) reminds once when `Assets/_Game/**/*.cs` changed without doc updates.

## Code style

- No XML/docstring blocks. At most one short `//` line on a method to state its purpose; skip it when the name is self-explanatory.
- Don't add comments narrating a fix or adjustment ("changed X to Y", "fixed bug"). Comment only for important/critical fixes, workarounds, or non-obvious solutions, and explain the *why*.

## Conventions / gotchas

- Commit messages in history use the style `+ add <thing>` (e.g. `+ add synty prototype`).
- `.gitattributes` is the standard Unity template with Git LFS for binary asset types; make sure LFS is installed before committing/pulling large assets.
- Always commit `.meta` files together with their assets; never delete/rename asset files outside the Unity Editor (or move the `.meta` alongside) or GUID references break.
- Main branch is `develop`.
